package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain malicious code in their __init__.py files that scans the user's filesystem for sensitive files and images, then exfiltrates both file paths and file contents to a Telegram bot controlled by cybercriminals. This is done without user consent, constituting a clear data theft operation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code recursively scans the root and DCIM directories for files with .py, .php, .zip, .png, .jpg, and .jpeg extensions, then exfiltrates both file paths and file contents to a hardcoded Telegram bot via HTTPS POST, resulting in unauthorized data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs broad filesystem scanning and exfiltrates potentially sensitive files and images to an external server (Telegram bot) without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages should not scan arbitrary directories or exfiltrate user files on import. Legitimate packages may read files, but only as part of explicit user actions and never send them to third-party servers without consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities or cloud sync tools may upload user files, but only after explicit user configuration and authentication.
key_indicators: Filesystem scan of root and DCIM directories
Collection of code, archive, and image files
Hardcoded Telegram bot token and chat ID
Automated exfiltration of files via network requests
Execution at import-time (no user interaction required)

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering code execution.
Malicious code scans root and DCIM directories for files with specific extensions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of file paths and file contents.

attack_chain.action: Collected files and their paths are exfiltrated to a Telegram bot via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data; user is compromised.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or install-time filesystem scanning of user directories
Automated exfiltration of files to external network endpoints (especially Telegram API)
Presence of hardcoded bot tokens or chat IDs in package code
file_indicators: __init__.py containing os.walk or recursive directory traversal
References to /DCIM or root directory scanning
network_indicators: Unusual traffic to Telegram API endpoints from development environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that perform filesystem scans and network requests at import or install time, especially those targeting broad directories like / or /DCIM. Flag packages containing hardcoded Telegram bot tokens or chat IDs, and inspect for code that posts files to api.telegram.org. Use static analysis to detect os.walk usage in __init__.py and dynamic analysis to observe unexpected network activity during package import.
